english: For positive integers $p$ and $q$, consider the arithmetic progressions $7,\ 7+p,\ 7+2p,\ \dots$ and $7,\ 7+q,\ 7+2q,\ \dots$. Let $S$ be the set of all ordered pairs $(p,q)$ for which the numbers common to the two progressions form an arithmetic progression with common difference $36$. Then the arithmetic mean of the numbers $p+q$, taken over all pairs $(p,q)\in S$, is ______.
hindi: धनात्मक पूर्णांकों $p$ तथा $q$ के लिए समान्तर श्रेढ़ियों $7,\ 7+p,\ 7+2p,\ \dots$ तथा $7,\ 7+q,\ 7+2q,\ \dots$ पर विचार कीजिए। माना $S$ उन सभी क्रमित युग्मों $(p,q)$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए दोनों श्रेढ़ियों में उभयनिष्ठ संख्याएँ $36$ सार्व अन्तर वाली एक समान्तर श्रेढ़ी बनाती हैं। तब सभी युग्मों $(p,q)\in S$ पर ली गई संख्याओं $p+q$ का समान्तर माध्य ______ है।
solution: $7+N$ is common iff $p\mid N$ and $q\mid N$, i.e. $\mathrm{lcm}(p,q)\mid N$: common terms form an AP with difference $\mathrm{lcm}(p,q)$
So $S=\{(p,q):\mathrm{lcm}(p,q)=36=2^2\cdot3^2\}$; for each prime the exponent pair has maximum $2$: $5$ choices, $|S|=25$
For $p=2^i3^j$ the number of partners $q$ is $c_ic_j$ with $c_0=c_1=1,\ c_2=3$
solution_full: A number $7+N$ ($N\ge0$) is a term of the first progression iff $p\mid N$, and of the second iff $q\mid N$. So it is common iff $\mathrm{lcm}(p,q)\mid N$, and the common terms are $7,\ 7+L,\ 7+2L,\dots$ with $L=\mathrm{lcm}(p,q)$.
Hence $(p,q)\in S$ exactly when $\mathrm{lcm}(p,q)=36=2^2\cdot3^2$; in particular $p\mid36$ and $q\mid36$.
Write $p=2^{i}3^{j}$ and $q=2^{k}3^{l}$ with exponents in $\{0,1,2\}$. The condition is $\max(i,k)=2$ and $\max(j,l)=2$.
For the prime $2$ the pairs $(i,k)$ with maximum $2$ are $(2,0),(2,1),(2,2),(0,2),(1,2)$: five; the same for the prime $3$. So $|S|=25$.
Fix $p=2^i3^j$. If $i=2$, $k$ can be $0,1,2$ (3 choices); if $i<2$, $k=2$ (1 choice). So the number of $q$ is $c_ic_j$ with $c_0=c_1=1$, $c_2=3$.
The set $S$ is symmetric in $p$ and $q$, so $\displaystyle\sum_S q=465$ too, and the mean of $p+q$ is $\dfrac{465+465}{25}=37.2$.
originality_note: New: the common difference of the common-term AP is prescribed, which turns into lcm(p, q) = 36, and the asked quantity is an average over all such pairs computed by a multiplicative weighting (way 5: common terms of APs linked with LCM counting). Closest known: 'number of ordered pairs with lcm(p, q) = n' and 'common terms of two APs' exercises. Different because: the LCM condition is hidden in the AP statement, and the answer needs a weighted sum over pairs rather than a count.

concept_use.Common terms of 2 or more Aps: The common terms of the two progressions form an AP with common difference lcm(p, q), which turns the condition into lcm(p, q) = 36.
concept_use.Counting ordered pairs with a given GCD: Counting ordered pairs with lcm 36 by prime exponents (5 x 5 = 25) and weighting each p by its number of partners gives the sum 465.
